key_insight: Equivalent quantum circuits can lose high-level synthesis choices during serialization or compiler interchange, so functional equivalence does not guarantee the same optimized gate decomposition.
engineering_relevance: Quantum compiler and workflow designers need to preserve or verify high-level operations across tool boundaries, or they risk worse gate counts and lost optimization control.
method: Compared Qiskit, TKET, and Cirq under controlled experiments, repository analysis, and circuits from project tests.
Tested serialization, OpenQASM interchange, compiler conversion, and an MQT pipeline to track when synthesis availability survives or disappears.
Introduced Verified, which records high-level ops before conversion and reconstructs them only after a consistency check passes.
evidence_signal: In the abstract’s evaluation, direct OpenQASM 3 round trips eliminated the effect of requested synthesis in all 360 delivered conditions, and Verified restored requested synthesis in all 830 recovery runs.
watch_item: Verified rejects stale records but also some valid ones, so its safety check can reduce applicability or require careful integration.
paper_title: When Equivalent Quantum Circuits Lose Synthesis Choices
